title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. Each stratum is replaced by a space Σ_i, i in the poset I of strata, thought of as the stratum with a deleted conic neighbourhood. For i<j there is Σ_ij, the 'link bundle' of stratum i inside stratum j. It comes with s_ij: Σ_ij → Σ_i (projection of the link bundle) and b_ij: Σ_ij → Σ_j (inclusion as a boundary piece). The previous page packages this as Σ = ∐Σ_i and Σ^(1) = ∐_{i<j}Σ_ij, with (s,b): Σ^(1) → Σ×Σ. Conditions a)-c) say this is the graph of a strict order with locally totally ordered predecessor sets. Condition d) says the Σ_ji (j in I_{<i,x}) are mutually transverse boundary subspaces at x.

(1) This page first states that d) makes the 'ordered topological space' structure satisfy condition c) of the Scholie (p.27).

(2) It then names special cases:
- Equisingular case: the s_ij are proper fibrations. This is Thom-Mather local triviality of link bundles.
- Non-singular case: the Σ_i are topological manifolds whose boundary is the union of the Σ_ji, j<i, i.e. manifolds with corners/faces. A margin note says the Σ_ij should themselves be manifolds with boundary, with boundary the union of Σ_kij and Σ_ikj, 'but one needs precise compatibility conditions...'. So triple-index link data Σ_ijk appears, and the compatibility is left open.
- Equisingular plus non-singular case: s_ij is a proper fibration whose fibres are manifolds with boundary, and the fibrewise boundary is the union of the Σ_ijh. In modern terms this is a manifold with fibred corners / iterated fibration structure.

(3) Digression B. Drop I and generalize to a topological category Σ:
- objects Σ_(0) and arrows Σ_(1), with s,b: Σ_(1) ⇉ Σ_(0);
- Σ_(2) = Σ_(1) ×_{b,Σ_(0),s} Σ_(1) with composition, and s a fibration.
Claim: I := π_0(Σ_(0)) is preordered ('ordonné' corrected to 'préordonné'). The relation is the image of π_0(Σ_(1)) → π_0(Σ_(0)×Σ_(0)) ≅ π_0(Σ_(0))².

The next page completes the argument:
- reflexivity comes from identities;
- transitivity comes from surjectivity of π_0(Σ_(2)) → π_0(Σ_(1)) ×_{π_0Σ_(0)} π_0(Σ_(1)), via a lemma: π_0 of a pullback along a fibration surjects onto the fibre product of π_0's;
- this yields a functor Σ → I to the poset viewed as a discrete topological category, i.e. decompositions Σ_(0) = ∐Σ_i and Σ_(1) = ∐_{i≤j}Σ_ij compatible with s,b.

The purpose is to recover the stratification poset and the unfolding data intrinsically from a topological category whose arrows are 'link points', a categorical model of stratified spaces.
errors: Gap: to get decompositions Σ_(0) = ∐_{i∈π_0}Σ_i with continuous maps to the discrete set I, path components must be open (e.g. local path-connectedness); this is not stated (possibly what the next page's margin 'NB' addresses).

Minor inconsistency: this page assumes s fibrant, while the next page invokes 'b fibrant'. Either suffices for the π_0-surjectivity of Σ_(2) by the lemma applied to the appropriate projection, so it is harmless.
Grothendieck himself corrects 'ordonné' to 'préordonné': antisymmetry is not automatic for a general topological category. Correct as amended.
The compatibility conditions for corners in the non-singular case are explicitly left unformulated ('il faut des conditions de compatibilité précisément...').

ideas.what: Unfolding of a stratified space into a system of spaces Σ_i (strata minus conic neighbourhoods) and link bundles Σ_ij with projection s and boundary inclusion b
ideas.modern_name: resolution/unzipping of a stratified space; manifolds with fibred corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goresky (1978), Verona (1984), Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza and Albin-Melrose (2010s), Ayala-Francis-Tanaka 'unzipping' (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6, sketch of 'déploiement' of stratified structures, without these axioms

ideas.what: Equisingular case = link projections are proper fibrations
ideas.modern_name: Thom-Mather local triviality / Thom's first isotopy lemma

ideas.what: Non-singular case: strata are manifolds whose boundary is a union of transverse faces Σ_ji, with fibrewise-boundary condition on link fibrations
ideas.modern_name: manifolds with corners / ⟨k⟩-manifolds; iterated fibration structures

ideas.what: Topological category with fibrant source map; π_0 of objects is preordered by the image of π_0 of arrows; a canonical functor to the poset gives a stratification-like decomposition
ideas.modern_name: stratification as a functor from an (exit-path-type) category to a poset; category objects presenting exit-path ∞-categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s), Treumann (2009), Woolf (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (2017)

ideas.what: Lemma: for a cartesian square with f a fibration, π_0(X') → π_0(X) ×_{π_0Y} π_0(Y') is surjective
ideas.modern_name: path-lifting / exactness of π_0 for homotopy pullbacks

missed.claim: Grothendieck models the unfolded stratified space as a topological category: objects = points of strata, arrows = points of link bundles, with source map a fibration. He recovers the stratifying poset as the π_0-preorder and the stratification as a functor to that poset. This anticipates the later viewpoint that stratified spaces correspond to (exit-path) categories with a conservative functor to a poset. It also anticipates presenting Exit(X) via the unzipped links (Ayala-Francis-Tanaka). The explicit link between the corner/link-bundle resolution and a category object with fibrant structure maps seems not credited to him.
missed.quote: considérons une catégorie topologique Σ = (Σ_(0)=Ob(Σ), Σ_(1)=Fl(Σ) ...) et supposons que s : Σ_(1) → Σ_(0) soit fibrant. Je dis qu'alors π_0(Σ_(0)) = I est un ens. préordonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early (1981-82) instance of the 'stratified space = category over a poset' paradigm. It uses a strict topological category with fibrancy rather than ∞-categories, and could give a point-set presentation of exit-path categories via link bundles.

missed.claim: Compatibility conditions for higher link data Σ_ijk in the non-singular (corner) case are left explicitly unformulated.
missed.quote: On demande que les Σ_ij soient des variétés à bord, que le bord soit réunion des Σ_kij et Σ_ikj — mais il faut des conditions de compatibilité précisément...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These conditions were later supplied as the axioms of manifolds with fibred corners / iterated fibration structures. Nothing here goes beyond them.

deep.surprise_reason: The unfolding into manifolds with corners and link bundles is known (Goresky, Verona, ALMP, AFT) and sketched in the Esquisse. The topological-category reformulation, recovering the strata poset as a π_0-preorder under a fibrancy hypothesis, is a modestly notable anticipation of the exit-path/category-over-poset viewpoint, but it is elementary and incomplete on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'ellipsoïdale [?] topologique ordonnée' is more likely 'd'espace top. ordonné' (structure d'espace topologique ordonné).
'condition c) de Schreier [?] (p. 27)' is likely 'condition c) du Scholie (p. 27)'.
The third heading is 'Cas équisingulier-non-singulier' (both cases combined), with corrections, not merely 'Cas non singulier'.
In the last case the indices of s_ij : Σ_?? → Σ_? are heavily corrected in the image. 'Σ_ijk → Σ_jk' is uncertain; it may read s_ij : Σ_ik → Σ_i-type maps.
In 'les Σ_ki sont des variétés' the index is probably Σ_i (strata), not Σ_ki.
The margin likely reads 'On voudrait que les Σ_ij soient des variétés à bord, que le bord soit réunion des Σ_kij et Σ_ikj — mais il faut des conditions de compatibilité précisément...'.
